claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT can predict and verify the presence of a ferromagnetic ground state in a material.
Energetically favorable spin-polarized configurations indicate a ferromagnetic ground state.
The candidate material has a non-spin-polarized, paramagnetic electronic configuration according to non-spin-polarized DFT.
Spin-polarized DFT calculations should incorporate an appropriate exchange-correlation functional.
The proposed calculations represent low-temperature conditions.
The proposed calculations assume a pristine crystalline structure.
The atomic lattice and electron exchange interactions mediate spin alignment.
Exchange interactions cause spin-splitting of the electronic states.
Adopting ferromagnetic ordering lowers the total energy through exchange-driven spin-splitting.
The exchange-driven reduction in total energy makes the spin-polarized ferromagnetic state the energetically favorable ground state.
The ferromagnetic configuration will have a lower total energy than the non-spin-polarized configuration.
The ferromagnetic configuration will have a non-zero net magnetic moment.
The non-spin-polarized baseline has no net magnetic moment.
The validity of the DFT prediction depends on the chosen exchange-correlation functional.
DFT may fail to capture all relevant many-body effects.
Experimental verification may be necessary to establish the magnetic ground state.
A non-spin-polarized energy less than or equal to the ferromagnetic energy would falsify the proposed ferromagnetic-ground-state prediction.
Absence of a net magnetic moment despite predicted spin-splitting would falsify the hypothesis.
